panels.visual: Young Plato, a broad-shouldered wrestler, pinning an opponent in a wrestling school, crowd cheering
panels.caption: Plato was born in Athens around 428 BC, into a rich family. They say he was a champion wrestler.

panels.visual: Plato in the Agora listening to barefoot old Socrates, then throwing his own scrolls of poems into a fire
panels.caption: Then he met Socrates, and burned the plays he had been writing so he could follow him.

panels.visual: Plato weeping as Socrates drinks the hemlock in prison, friends around
panels.caption: When Athens put Socrates to death in 399 BC, Plato was heartbroken, and left the city for years.

panels.visual: Plato walking out of the city gate along a road to a green grove of olive trees
panels.caption: When he came back, he walked out of the city to an olive grove sacred to a hero called Akademos.

panels.visual: Plato teaching students under olive trees, drawing triangles and circles in the sand with a stick
panels.caption: Around 387 BC he started a school there. People called it the Academy, after the grove.

panels.visual: A neat young student with rings (Aristotle) arguing with Plato, both smiling
panels.caption: Bright young people came from all over Greece. One student, Aristotle, stayed twenty years.

panels.visual: Two young women among the students, one wearing a man's cloak, listening closely
panels.caption: Two women, Axiothea and Lasthenia, studied there too. One old story says Axiothea dressed like a man.

panels.visual: A stone sign over a doorway reading LET NO ONE IGNORANT OF GEOMETRY ENTER, a big question mark beside it
panels.caption: A story says a sign over the door read this. Nobody mentions it until centuries later.

panels.visual: The school under the olive trees over many generations, teachers grey-haired and new students arriving
panels.caption: The school went on for hundreds of years after Plato died.

panels.visual: AD 529: a Byzantine emperor (Justinian, crown, purple robes) signing a decree; philosophers packing up scrolls
panels.caption: In AD 529 the emperor Justinian banned pagans from teaching. The old schools closed.

panels.visual: Today: a modern city park with olive trees and low stone ruins behind fences, apartment blocks around, children playing
panels.caption: Today the Academy is a park in a busy neighbourhood, two kilometres from the Agora. Only low ruins are left.

panels.visual: A modern school building with a sign ACADEMY, Glauka the owl perched on the sign
panels.caption: Every academy in the world is named after this olive grove.
